en.answer: Heating increases particle energy; during phase change energy is used to overcome attractions, changing arrangement and freedom of movement.

en.stem: Define isotopes.
en.answer: Atoms of the same element with the same proton number but different neutron numbers.

en.stem: Explain atomic number and mass number.
en.answer: Atomic number is proton count; mass number is protons plus neutrons; a neutral atom has equal protons and electrons.

en.stem: What is a covalent bond?
en.answer: A bond formed by sharing one or more electron pairs between atoms.

en.stem: Compare ionic and covalent bonding.
en.answer: Ionic bonding involves electron transfer and electrostatic attraction between ions; covalent bonding involves shared electron pairs.

en.stem: Compare exothermic and endothermic reactions.

en.stem: Why is equilibrium called dynamic?
en.answer: Forward and reverse reactions continue microscopically at equal rates while macroscopic concentrations remain constant.

en.stem: Explain how a change in concentration or temperature can shift equilibrium.
